# ZViewer

> ZViewer is an offline native Android comic reader for local archives (ZIP/CBZ, RAR/CBR, 7Z), PDF, image folders, and video folders, built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.

ZViewer (`dev.zolive.zviewer`) targets Android 10+ (minSdk 29, compile/target SDK 36) and ships a universal APK for `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64`. All content is processed on-device: the release manifest requests no network, external-storage, or all-files permissions, and uses a Storage Access Framework (SAF) persistent read grant for a user-selected library folder. The UI and Chinese docs are written in Simplified Chinese. Current version: 1.4.0 (`versionCode 10`). License: MIT.

## Features

- Comic sources: ZIP / CBZ, RAR / CBR, 7Z (via libarchive), PDF (via `PdfRenderer`), image folders, and video folders or video-only archives.
- Static images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, HEIF, HEIC, AVIF.
- Animated images: APNG, animated WebP, GIF, animated AVIF (via APNG4Android + libavif).
- Library: recursive scan, natural filename sorting (`2.jpg` before `10.jpg`), HD covers, search, reading-status filter, recently read, favorites, 2–5 column grid.
- Reader: continuous vertical or paged horizontal images with adjacent loop boundaries; smooth finger-following video switching (the settled page and its immediate neighbours each keep a preloaded player, so an incoming video has already rendered its saved-position first frame before it slides in; the current video keeps playing until the page settles; if the outgoing video ends mid-transition it loops); mixed image/video books follow the vertical/horizontal reading setting and show the seek slider only on video pages; a finished video replays from the start when revisited after auto-advancing; per-video positions, pinch and double-tap zoom, toolbar play/pause and seek slider, page/video-number jump, keep screen on; an optional diagnostic log can be written to the default app directory or a user-picked SAF folder. Codec support depends on the device's Media3 / system decoders.
- Appearance: follow-system / light / dark theme, preset or custom accent color, independent light/dark reading backgrounds.
- Storage: manual cache clearing plus automatic reclamation at ~1.5 GiB.

## Supported Formats

| Kind | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Archives | `zip`, `cbz`, `rar`, `cbr`, `7z` |
| Documents | `pdf` |
| Static images | `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `bmp`, `heif`, `heic`, `avif` |
| Animated images | `apng`, animated `webp`, `gif`, animated `avif` |
| Video | `mp4`, `m4v`, `mkv`, `webm`, `avi`, `mov`, `3gp`, `3g2`, `mpg`, `mpeg`, `ts`, `mts`, `m2ts`, `flv`, `wmv`, `ogv`, `vob`, `rm`, `rmvb` |

Not supported: encrypted or multi-volume archives, password-protected PDFs, DRM content, animated HEIF. Solid 7Z archives require preparing the whole book on first open.

## Architecture

- `app/src/main/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/MainActivity.kt` — single Activity, edge-to-edge Compose host.
- `LibraryViewModel.kt` — app state, SAF folder selection, scan/open jobs, error mapping, settings and progress.
- `data/PreferenceStore.kt` — SharedPreferences persistence for tree URI, book index JSON, page/video progress, favorites, settings, and the diagnostic-log options.
- `data/DiagnosticLog.kt` — optional in-app diagnostic logging. When enabled it appends app start, device info, app lifecycle, library scan/open, video prepare/buffering/ready/ended, play-when-ready and is-playing changes, video and surface sizes, first-frame rendering, surface-ownership handovers, playback-gate decisions, the player pool, cover extraction timing, and uncaught exceptions to a per-process `zviewer-<date>-<time>.log`. It defaults to the app-specific external `logs/` directory (no permission) and can be pointed at a user-picked SAF directory such as Download (only that tree's persisted read/write grant is held; no all-files access). Writes are serialized on an IO coroutine and the crash handler flushes synchronously; an unwritable directory falls back to the default one.
- `data/BookRepository.kt` — `DocumentsContract` bulk queries, background extraction, PDF rendering, video preparation, cover and page caches; enforces safety limits.
- `data/Models.kt` — `Book`, `BookSession`, media-aware `PageSource`, `ReadingProgress`, `ReaderSettings`, `NaturalOrder`, `ReaderException`.
- `reader/ImageLoader.kt` — PNG-chunk APNG detection, AVIF via APNG4Android + libavif, other formats via `ImageDecoder`, sampled animation wrapper.
- `reader/ZoomImageView.kt` — native matrix zoom/pan in an `AndroidView`; unzoomed gestures pass through to Compose lists/pager.
- `ui/LibraryScreen.kt` — `ZViewerApp` entry, library grid, search/filter, continue-reading card.
- `reader/ReaderPaging.kt` — virtual loop positions mapped to real page numbers for LazyColumn / HorizontalPager.
- `reader/ZoomVideoView.kt` — Android gesture detection, zoom/pan, a cached first-frame cover under the Media3 TextureView, and unzoomed drags passed through to the surrounding Compose Pager.
- `ui/ReaderScreen.kt`, `ui/VideoReader.kt` — image reader and Media3 video playback with shared toolbar visibility, play/pause, a seek slider, and optional diagnostic logging. All video books (pure and mixed) use the same Compose Pager in the user's vertical or horizontal direction: a finger-following drag keeps the settled video playing while the incoming page is already showing its live frame. Players are preloaded for the settled page and its two immediate neighbours (at most three); each neighbour renders its saved-position first frame into its own TextureView while off-screen, so a swipe never creates or destroys a surface mid-gesture and cannot flash. Players are retained while their page stays inside the Pager composition window and released when the page moves two or more positions away (or leaves the composition), so an aborted drag or repeated back-and-forth keeps the same player instance; looping duplicate virtual items are never all given players. Farther pages (including duplicates) are cover-only from a small session-level LRU cover cache. Every video page keeps the same `AndroidView` structure whether or not it currently has a player, so switching cannot flash between a cover view and a player view. Each player has a single owning view: ownership is transferred by detaching the previous view before binding the replacement, stale views cannot clear the live surface, and releasing a transient duplicate falls back to the still-settled view. Playback additionally requires the owning view's TextureView surface to be attached; without it the player pauses until the surface returns. Media3's black shutter is made transparent and the cached cover always sits behind the video, so the cover shows until the opaque first frame covers it without toggling visibility; the buffering spinner only appears on the settled page before its first frame is rendered. `repeatMode` is set only from the single-video-loop / loop-mode settings and never toggled by scrolling or transitions: ExoPlayer re-initializes its decoder output when the repeat mode changes near the end of a clip (video size drops to 0x0 and the first frame is re-rendered), which caused a visible flash; a video that ends mid-transition is replayed from the start by the `onEnded` callback instead. Reactivating an ended player also seeks back to the start and honors the preview setting. Video folders play directly from SAF URIs; video archive members use extracted files. Covers use MediaMetadataRetriever to sample the naturally sorted first video; per-page first-frame covers are cached per session and retried once on failure.
- `ui/SettingsScreen.kt`, `ui/Theme.kt` — Material 3 settings and theming.

Data flow: user picks a folder → SAF persistent read permission → background recursive scan → book index → cover generated on demand → book opened → image pages decoded or video members extracted → visible media played → page/video number and video position saved.

## Privacy and Security

- No `INTERNET`, external-storage read/write, or `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission; no accounts, ads, or telemetry.
- Only the user-granted directory is read; original comic files are never modified, moved, or deleted.
- Backups and device-to-device migration are disabled so URI grants do not migrate with app data.
- Archive members are written to app-generated sequential filenames; hidden files, macOS metadata (`.`, `__MACOSX`), symlinks, and unsupported entries are skipped. Member names are decoded as UTF-8 (`Archive.setCharset` overrides Android's C locale) so Chinese filenames do not raise ARCHIVE_WARN. An archive containing both images and videos opens as a mixed horizontal book. Any readable archive containing a PDF reports that PDFs must be extracted before reading, including mixed archives; parser failures retain the corrupt/archive error path.
- Safety limits: 20,000 pages per comic, 256 MB per image, 4 GB extracted per book, archive scan recursion depth 32.

## Build and Test

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK 36, network access for dependency download, Gradle 8.11.1 wrapper (bundled).

```sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android"
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug
./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest              # device format integration tests
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease                          # signed release build
```

- Unit tests: `app/src/test/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/data/NaturalOrderTest.kt` (natural ordering, hidden-file filtering, cache keys, image extensions).
- Paging tests: `app/src/test/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/reader/ReaderPagingTest.kt` (both loop boundaries, repeated cycles, single-page books, large page counts).
- Video and gesture regression tests: `VideoIntegrationTest.kt`, `ReaderInteractionTest.kt` in `app/src/androidTest/`; video samples are generated by `python3 tools/generate_video_fixtures.py` using FFmpeg.
- Instrumented tests: `app/src/androidTest/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/FormatIntegrationTest.kt` covering CBZ/ZIP, RAR4/CBR, RAR5, 7Z, PDF, image folders, HEIF/HEIC/AVIF, animated formats, corrupt/empty archives, path traversal, and a 4800×3200 APNG.
- Fixtures: generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py`; `tools/ui_smoke.py` replays most manual UI flows.
- Release signing: key `.signing/zviewer-release.jks` (alias `zviewer`), passwords from `ZVIEWER_STORE_PASSWORD` / `ZVIEWER_KEY_PASSWORD`; output `app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`. Never commit `.signing/`.
- Distributed APKs live in `dist/` with SHA-256 checksums (e.g. `ZViewer-1.4.0-release.apk`).

## Key Dependencies

`androidx.compose:compose-bom:2025.05.01`, `androidx.activity:activity-compose:1.10.1`, `androidx.lifecycle:*:2.9.0`, `androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer:1.6.1` and `:media3-ui:1.6.1`, Kotlin coroutines 1.10.2, `me.zhanghai.android.libarchive:library:1.1.6`, `com.github.penfeizhou.android.animation:apng:3.0.5` and `:avif:3.0.5`, `org.aomedia.avif.android:avif:1.3.0.841110fd`. Android framework gestures and thumbnail extraction use AOSP APIs (Apache 2.0).
